title: Set out an exam room: every desk facing the front, 1.25 m apart centre to centre
instruction: Set this classroom out for a written exam (1:10 scale). Move and turn the four desks, each with its chair fixed behind it, so that every candidate would face the front of the room (the whiteboard and the clock), each desk square to the front wall within 15 degrees, and no two desks are closer than 125 mm (1.25 m) centre to centre in any direction, measured between the middles of the desk tops. Leave every desk standing upright on the grey floor.
context: School site staff, exams officers and invigilators in the UK set rooms out for written exams to the Joint Council for Qualifications' Instructions for Conducting Examinations (JCQ ICE): every candidate facing the same direction, and at least 1.25 m between the centres of neighbouring desks in every direction, so that no candidate can read another's script. Rooms are normally turned to face the front, where the clock and the exam times are displayed for every candidate to see. The same classrooms are used for group or seminar work, so turning a room round is routine before every mock and exam series. Here a 1:10 classroom holds four single desks, each with its chair fixed behind it (so each unit shows which way its candidate faces), left as a seminar had them: two rows facing each other across the room. Each desk must be turned a quarter turn the right way, not round to face the back, and spread to the spacing.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 1:10 classroom stands on the table. Fixed: (1) Floor: a mid-grey vinyl sheet 1 mm thick, x 15.0 to 46.0 cm, y -28.0 to +28.0 cm (3.1 x 5.6 m). (2) Front wall: off-white painted MDF 10 mm thick and 60 mm tall (cut down so the camera sees the room), x 46.0 to 47.0 cm, y -28.0 to +28.0 cm, standing on the table along the floor's far edge; its face (the room side) is at x 46.0 cm. (3) On the wall's face: a whiteboard (white card 2 mm thick, y -15.0 to +15.0 cm, 15 to 55 mm up) and the exam clock (a black plastic square 30 x 30 mm, 3 mm thick, with a 24 mm white card face 1 mm thick, centred at y +20.0 cm, 35 mm up). Loose: (4) Four desk units, each one rigid 80 g body: a single desk with a beech-effect laminate top 60 mm wide, 45 mm deep and 6 mm thick, its top face 72 mm up, on two grey steel side frames 6 mm thick, 45 mm deep and 66 mm tall, flush with the top's left and right edges; and a chair fixed behind the desk by a grey steel rail (4 x 48 x 6 mm, between the side frames' back ends, 40 to 46 mm up): a blue polypropylene seat 36 mm wide, 32 mm deep and 6 mm thick, its top 46 mm up, on two grey steel side frames 4 x 32 x 40 mm, and a blue back 36 mm wide and 5 mm thick along the seat's back edge, from the seat up to 86 mm. The whole unit is 60 mm wide, 77 mm deep and 86 mm tall. A unit faces the way a candidate on its chair would: from the chair toward the desk. A desk's centre is the middle of its top. Start (a seminar layout: all four standing upright on the floor in two rows facing each other across the middle of the room, each row's two desks 100 mm apart centre to centre, 40 mm between their side frames): desk 1 centred at x 26.0 cm, y +20.0 cm and desk 2 at x 36.0 cm, y +20.0 cm, both facing -y (chairs toward +y); desk 3 at x 26.0 cm, y -20.0 cm and desk 4 at x 36.0 cm, y -20.0 cm, both facing +y (chairs toward -y). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The score is read from the four desks' poses at the last step, as a top photo with a tape and a protractor would read it. A desk faces from its chair toward its desk, seen from above; its centre is the middle of its desk top. A desk is set when it is tilted 10 degrees or less, its lowest point is within 3 mm of the floor, its centre is over the grey floor (seen from above; the edge counts) and it is still (moved under 5 mm over the last 0.5 s, turns counted at its farthest corner). It faces the front when it faces within 15 degrees of square to the front wall (+x, toward the whiteboard and the clock). It is spaced when its centre is at least 125 mm (1.25 m), seen from above, from the centre of every other desk, set or not: a tipped, lifted or sideways desk still takes up its place. Score: 0.25 for each desk that is set, faces the front and is spaced: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. The desks are alike, so any desk may go anywhere. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s. Examples: the start (all four facing sideways, each row's two desks 100 mm apart) 0; a 2 x 2 grid all facing the front, 160 mm apart front to back and 300 mm across, 1.0; the same with one desk turned round to face the back, or left facing sideways, 0.75; two desks facing the front but 100 mm apart (neither counts) and the other two right 0.5; one starting row's two desks done and the other row untouched 0.5; one desk right and the rest as they started 0.25; all four facing the front in a tight block 100 mm apart 0; spread out but all facing a side wall 0. A desk on its side, held more than 3 mm up, stacked on another or with its centre off the floor earns nothing, and still counts as a neighbour in the others' spacing. Score 0 if no desk is set, facing the front and spaced. In a real trial, read once nothing moves: a tape between pencil dots at the middles of the desk tops on a top photo, a protractor against the line of the front wall for the facing, and a 3 mm feeler gauge, which must not pass under a set desk.
fidelity: A 1:10 model, default friction. Floor, wall, whiteboard and clock are fixed; each desk unit is one 80 g rigid body of boxes, with no candidate or papers. Each chair is fixed behind its desk, as in combination desk-and-chair units, so the unit shows which way it faces (loose chairs are more usual). Only the front wall is modelled, cut to 60 mm so the camera sees in; the floor's edges mark the room. The scorer sees only the desks: one held still within 3 mm of the floor counts as set.
reset_notes: Stand the four desk units upright on the grey floor as they started: desk 1 centred at x 26.0 cm, y +20.0 cm and desk 2 at x 36.0 cm, y +20.0 cm, both facing -y (chairs toward +y); desk 3 at x 26.0 cm, y -20.0 cm and desk 4 at x 36.0 cm, y -20.0 cm, both facing +y (chairs toward -y). A desk's centre is the middle of its top. The floor, wall, whiteboard and clock are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
